skill.name: bilig-workpaper
skill.description: Run file-backed WorkPaper spreadsheet formula workflows with @bilig/headless, MCP tools, and TypeScript without automating Excel.

skill.author: proompteng

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown backticks, inline tool names, safety text, or documentation links. Two findings are confirmed because the skill runs npm exec for MCP and formula clinic commands. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed skill text.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before npm exec and recommend preinstalling a reviewed @bilig/headless version from a trusted lockfile.
Keep writable mode opt-in, validate workpaper paths, and restrict writes to user-approved workspace files.
State that linked documentation is optional and should not be fetched with private workbook data.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet formula work is hard to verify when agents avoid desktop Excel. This skill guides file-backed WorkPaper edits, MCP tools, TypeScript usage, and local formula reports.
actual_capabilities: Configures a bilig-workpaper MCP server with npm exec and argument arrays.
Lists and reads workbook sheets, ranges, and cells through file-backed MCP tools.
Writes cell contents and reads recalculated display values after changes.
Shows direct TypeScript usage for building WorkPaper state and exporting documents.
Generates local XLSX formula clinic reports for reduced workbook issues.
limitations: It does not automate Excel desktop, VBA, pivots, charts, or COM features.
It depends on @bilig/headless compatibility for supported formulas.
It asks users to provide reduced public fixtures instead of private spreadsheets.
It requires local npm execution or a host that can run MCP stdio servers.

use_cases.title: Validate Pricing Formula Updates
use_cases.description: Analysts can update input cells, read recalculated outputs, and export WorkPaper evidence without opening desktop Excel.

use_cases.title: Embed Spreadsheet Logic in Services
use_cases.description: Developers can model spreadsheet-style formulas inside Node.js services, route handlers, or queue workers.

use_cases.title: Report XLSX Formula Bugs
use_cases.description: QA engineers can create local formula reports from reduced XLSX workbooks and cite unsupported behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect workbook outputs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing WorkPaper file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Bilig WorkPaper skill to list sheets in {workpaper_path}, read {input_range}, and read {output_cell}. Report current values.

prompt_templates.title: Update one input cell
prompt_templates.prompt: Open {workpaper_path} through MCP. Change {sheet}!{cell} from {old_value} to {new_value}, read {dependent_cell}, and export the document.

prompt_templates.title: Embed formula logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to use @bilig/headless in a TypeScript service for {business_model}. Include required sheets, inputs, formulas, and export verification.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare formula bug report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use a reduced workbook at {xlsx_path}. Run the formula clinic for {cells}, summarize mismatches, and list compatibility limits.

output_examples.input: Update Inputs!B2 from 20 to 32 and verify Summary!B2.
output_examples.output: Inputs!B2 changed from 20 to 32. Summary!B2 recalculated from 24000 to 38400. The WorkPaper export completed successfully.

output_examples.input: Check a reduced XLSX workbook for Summary!B7 and Inputs!B2.
output_examples.output: The local report compared the requested cells, listed formula support gaps, and identified which values need a smaller reproduction case.

output_examples.input: Review whether a WorkPaper model is ready for service use.
output_examples.output: The review identified required sheets, input cells, output cells, export steps, and unsupported Excel-only features.

best_practices: Validate workbook paths and cell references before running any local command.
Read dependent output cells after every write and include before and after values.
Use reduced public workbooks for bug reports and keep private spreadsheets out of fixtures.
anti_patterns: Do not concatenate user text into shell commands.
Do not claim a workbook changed without export or readback proof.
Do not use this skill for Excel desktop macros, VBA, charts, or pivots.

faq.question: Does this skill edit Excel files directly?
faq.answer: No. It works with Bilig WorkPaper state and reduced XLSX formula reports, not interactive Excel desktop editing.

faq.question: Can it run through Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the host can run local commands or MCP.

faq.question: Does it upload spreadsheet data?
faq.answer: No evidence in the skill shows uploads. The instructions say the formula clinic report is local.

faq.question: Why does it prefer argument arrays?
faq.answer: Argument arrays reduce shell injection risk when paths or cell references come from users.

faq.question: What proof should an agent return?
faq.answer: Return edited cells, before values, after values, export evidence, and limitations for unsupported formulas.

faq.question: What are the main security concerns?
faq.answer: It can run npm exec for @bilig/headless, so users should trust the package source and validate inputs.
